description: Typical crop duration and harvest-window assumptions for Indian conditions. Ranges are compiled from ICAR package-of-practices guidance and are deliberately configurable; they are planning aids, not a field diagnosis.
source: ICAR package of practices (typical ranges, 2024). Values are indicative and vary by variety, irrigation and region.

Rice.notes: Duration from transplanting/direct seeding to physiological maturity; drain field before harvest.

Wheat.notes: Harvest at 12-14% grain moisture; avoid delay after maturity to limit shattering.

Maize.notes: Cobs mature when husk turns dry; grain moisture should be below 15% for storage.

Cotton.notes: Picking is staged across multiple pickings; first picking typically starts 140-170 days after sowing.

Soyabean.notes: Harvest when pods turn brown and seed moisture is around 12-14%.

Groundnut.notes: Pod maturity indicated by darkened pod mesocarp; avoid over-maturity to reduce in-situ germination.

Onion.notes: Harvest after neck fall and cure bulbs in shade before storage or sale.

Tomato.notes: Harvest at breaker/pink stage for distant markets; multiple pickings are typical.

Potato.notes: Dehaulm 10-15 days before harvest to harden skin for storage.

Sugarcane.notes: Mill-maturity is assessed by sucrose content; coordinate with the sugar mill calendar.

Chickpea.notes: Harvest when pods turn brown and seed is hard.

Mustard.notes: Harvest when 75-80% siliquae turn yellow to limit shattering.

Chilli.notes: Red chilli harvest depends on colour development and dry matter; multiple pickings.

Banana.notes: Harvest at 75-80% maturity for distant markets; bunches are harvested in stages.

default.notes: No crop-specific calendar is configured; a 120-day generic assumption is used. Treat the estimate as low confidence.
